factual_claims.claim: Women are over-represented in administrative, clerical, and service jobs that are vulnerable to AI displacement.
AI systems trained on biased datasets have been documented to discriminate in hiring, lending, and healthcare.
Women are approximately 20% less likely than men to use generative AI tools.
Workplace adoption of AI among U.S. workers reached 46% in mid-2025.
AI systems improved from solving 4.4% of coding problems in 2023 to 71.7% in 2024.
Men's research productivity increased 6.4% more than women's following the release of ChatGPT.
Women consistently perceive AI to be riskier than men.
factual_claims.claim_label: Gender Gap in AI Risk Perception

factual_claims.claim: Women consistently exhibit lower risk orientation (higher risk aversion) than men.
Women face higher exposure to AI across both high-complementarity and high-substitution roles.
factual_claims.claim_label: Gender Gap in AI Risk Exposure

factual_claims.claim: Women are under-represented in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields.
Women are more supportive of government intervention to slow down AI adoption than men.
factual_claims.claim_label: Gender Gap in AI Regulation Support

factual_claims.claim: Men demonstrate higher objective knowledge of AI than women.
